content: Evidence and recommendations will be reviewed five years after the publication date to determine if updates are necessary. However, earlier reviews may be conducted if significant new evidence emerges that could alter the recommendations. Discussions among the Guideline Development Group (GDG) and the external review group have identified several areas where evidence is limited, necessitating further research to improve the control and elimination of schistosomiasis. These areas include: 1. Studies to establish indicators for measuring disease morbidity as progress is made toward eliminating schistosomiasis as a public health problem. 2. Research on optimal strategies for equitable treatment of various occupational groups, such as fishermen, farmers, irrigation workers, and car washers. 3. Investigations into the compliance of individuals taking praziquantel in areas where transmission has been reduced. 4. Development of new diagnostic tools for detecting Schistosoma species (S. haematobium and S. mansoni), particularly in the context of transmission interruption and the treatment of animals in endemic areas. 5. Monitoring drug efficacy to detect the emergence of drug resistance. 6. Studies on the safety of praziquantel during the first trimester of pregnancy, with appropriately sized sample populations. 7. Development of vaccines for humans and animals to prevent reinfection and reduce transmission. 8. Strategies for treatment in low-prevalence areas that do not require mass drug administration (MDA). 9. Research on improved diagnostic tests for animals and snails. 10. Operational research on persistent transmission hotspots, including their identification and control responses. 11. Studies on optimal treatment coverage across age groups for morbidity control, tailored to different transmission archetypes. 12. Research on seasonal targeting of interventions. 13. Comparisons of test-and-treat approaches versus mass drug administration (MDA). 14. Identification of circumstances where strategies should be tailored to include biannual treatment, snail control, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions. 15. Investigations into the role of hybrid schistosomes in transmission and diagnosis. 16. Further operational research in settings that compare school-based treatment with community-wide treatment. 17. Determination of optimal approaches for joint implementation of WASH interventions in highly endemic regions. 18. Development and evaluation of new, environmentally friendly molluscicides. These research priorities aim to address gaps in knowledge and improve strategies for the control and eventual elimination of schistosomiasis.
